﴿Is it a wonder to the people that We revealed to a man from among them: Warn the people?﴾ and ﴿Say: O people, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all.﴾

{47} ﴿And had it not been that a calamity should befall them for what their hands have put forward﴾: of disbelief and disobedience, they would have said: ﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your verses and be among the believers?﴾ That is, We have sent you, O Muhammad, to remove their argument and cut off their pretext.

{48} ﴿But when the truth came to them﴾: which is beyond doubt, ﴿from Us﴾: namely the Qur'an which We revealed to you. ﴿They said﴾: rejecting it and raising objections with what is not a valid objection: ﴿Why was he not given the like of what was given to Musa?﴾ That is, why was not a book sent down from heaven all at once? Now, as for the fact that it is sent down in installments, that does not show it is not from Allah. What proof is there in this? And what doubt is there that it is not from Allah merely because it was sent down piecemeal? Rather, part of the perfection of this Qur'an and of Allah's care for the one to whom it was sent is that it was sent down in parts, so that Allah might strengthen the heart of His Messenger through it, and that the faith of the believers might increase. ﴿And they do not bring you any example but We bring you the truth and the best explanation.﴾ Moreover, their analogy with the Book of Musa is an analogy they themselves have broken. How can they draw an analogy with a book which they disbelieved in and did not believe [in]? For this reason He said: ﴿Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Musa before? They said: Two kinds of magic supporting each other﴾; that is, the Qur'an and the Torah cooperate in their magic and in misleading people. ﴿And they said: Indeed we are disbelievers in both.﴾ Thus it is established by this that these people want to nullify the truth with what is not proof, and they refute it with what cannot be refuted, and they utter contradictory and varying statements. This is the condition of every disbeliever. For this reason He declared that they disbelieved in both books and both messengers.

{49} But is their disbelief in both of them a pursuit of truth and following of something they regard as better than both, or is it merely caprice? Allah the Exalted, binding them to this, said: ﴿Say: Then bring a book from Allah that is better guidance than both of them﴾; that is, better than the Torah and the Qur'an; ﴿I will follow it, if you are truthful.﴾ They have no way, nor does anyone else have a way, to bring the like of these two, for since Allah created the world no books have reached the world like these two in knowledge, guidance, clarity, and mercy to creation. This is from the perfection of fairness on the part of the caller, that he says: My aim is the truth, guidance, and right direction, and I have brought you this book which contains that and agrees with the Book of Musa. Therefore it is incumbent upon all of us to submit to both and follow them insofar as they are guidance and truth. If you bring me a book from Allah that is better guidance than them, I will follow it; otherwise I will not abandon a guidance and truth I know for something other than guidance and truth.

{50} ﴿But if they do not respond to you﴾: and do not bring a book better guidance than them, ﴿then know that they only follow their own desires﴾; that is, know that their abandonment of following you is not because they are going toward a truth they recognize or toward guidance, but is merely following their desires. ﴿And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah?﴾ This is one of the most astray of people, for guidance and the straight path that leads to Allah and to the abode of His honor were presented to him, yet he did not turn to it or incline to it, and his desire called him to take the paths leading to ruin and wretchedness, so he followed it and abandoned guidance. Is there anyone more astray than one described thus? But his wrongdoing, his transgression, and his lack of love for the truth are what made it necessary for him to remain in his error and for Allah not to guide him. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾; that is, those for whom wrongdoing has become a characteristic and obstinacy a description. Guidance came to them and they rejected it, desire presented itself to them and they followed it. They closed upon themselves the doors and paths of guidance, and opened upon themselves the doors and ways of misguidance. So they wander in their error and wrongdoing, and hesitate in their wretchedness and ruin. In His words ﴿But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their desires﴾ there is evidence that everyone who does not respond to the Messenger and goes to a statement contrary to the statement of the Messenger, has not gone to guidance but to desire.

{51} ﴿And We have certainly conveyed the word to them﴾; that is, We followed it up, connected it, and sent it down gradually, out of mercy and kindness toward them, ﴿so that they might remember﴾: when its verses are repeated upon them and its clear proofs descend upon them at the time they need them. Thus its piecemeal descent was a mercy to them. So why do they object to what is for their own benefit?

**Section on mentioning some benefits and lessons in this wondrous story**

Among them: the signs of Allah the Exalted, His lessons and His days among the earlier nations, are only benefited from and illuminated by believers. So a servant's lesson is in proportion to his faith. Allah the Exalted only relates these stories for their sake; as for others, Allah does not regard them, and they have no light or guidance from them.

Among them: when Allah the Exalted wills a matter, He prepares its causes and brings them about gradually, step by step, not all at once.

Among them: an oppressed nation, however weak it may be, should not be overcome by laziness in seeking its rights, nor by despair of rising to the highest matters, especially when they are wronged. Just as Allah rescued the nation of the Children of Israel, a weak nation, from the captivity of Pharaoh and his chiefs, and established them in the land and gave them their country as sovereigns.

Among them: as long as a nation is humiliated and subdued, not taking its right and not speaking it, its affairs of religion and worldly life will not be upheld, and it will have no leadership in them.

Among them: Allah's gentleness toward the mother of Musa, and His easing for her the calamity by the good news that Allah would return her son to her and make him one of the messengers.

Among them: Allah decrees for His servant some hardships in order to bring him greater joy than that, or to ward off from him a greater evil than it. As He decreed for the mother of Musa that intense grief and profound anxiety which was a means for her son to reach her in a way that would calm her soul, cool her eye, and increase her in happiness and joy.

Among them: natural fear of creatures does not contradict faith nor remove it, as happened to the mother of Musa and to Musa himself with those fears.

Among them: faith increases and decreases, and among the greatest things by which faith increases and certainty is completed is patience at times of disturbance and Allah's steadfastness at times of distress. As He said: ﴿Had We not strengthened her heart, she would have been among the believers﴾; that is, so that her faith would increase by that and her heart would be at rest.

Among them: among the greatest blessings of Allah upon His servant and the greatest help to a servant in his affairs is Allah's steadfastness toward him, and His binding of his composure and heart at times of fear and at bewildering matters. For by this he is enabled to speak the right word and do the right deed. Unlike one whose anxiety, terror, and agitation persist; his thinking is lost and his mind is stupefied, so he does not benefit himself in that state.

Among them: even if a servant knows that Allah's decree, destiny, and promise are binding and unavoidable, he should not neglect taking the causes he was commanded to take, and that does not contradict his belief in Allah's report. For Allah promised the mother of Musa that He would return him to her, yet she still strove to return him, and she sent his sister to follow him and seek him out.

Among them: it is permissible for a woman to go out for her needs and to speak with men without objection, as happened with the sister of Musa and the daughter of the man of Madyan.

Among them: it is permissible to take payment for nursing, fostering, and for guiding to one who does such work.

Among them: from Allah's mercy toward His weak servant whom He wishes to honor is that He shows him some of His signs and lets him witness some of His clear proofs, which increase his faith, as Allah returned Musa to his mother, so that she would know that Allah's promise is true.

Among them: it is not permissible to kill a disbeliever who has a covenant by contract or by custom. For Musa (peace be upon him) considered his killing of the Coptic disbeliever a sin, and asked Allah's forgiveness for it.

Among them: whoever kills souls without right is counted among the tyrants who spread corruption in the land.

Among them: whoever kills souls without right, and claims that he intends reform in the land and intimidation of the people of sin, is lying in that, and he is a corrupter. As Allah related the words of the Copt: ﴿You only want to be a tyrant in the land, and you do not want to be among the reformers﴾: in the sense of affirming it to him, not denying it.

Among them: a man informing another of what was said about him, in order to warn him of an evil he might fall into, is not tale-bearing (namimah); rather it may be obligatory, as that man informed Musa, advising and warning him.

Among them: if he fears killing and destruction in remaining, he should not throw himself into ruin nor submit to it, but should leave, as Musa did.

Among them: when two corruptions conflict, and one of them must be committed, he should commit the lighter and safer of the two, as when Musa's affair was between staying in Egypt where he would be killed, or going to distant lands whose road he did not know and had no guide except his Lord. But this situation was more hopeful for safety than the first, so Musa followed it.

Among them: a person examining knowledge when there is need to speak about it, if he has not found one of the two opinions preponderant, should seek guidance from his Lord and ask Him to guide him to the correct one of the two, after intending the truth in his heart and searching for it. For Allah does not disappoint one in this condition, as Musa went out toward Madyan and said: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way.﴾

Among them: compassion toward creation and kindness to those who know and those who do not know are among the characteristics of the prophets, and that among kindness is giving water to livestock and helping the weak.

Among them: it is recommended to make supplication by clarifying and explaining one's condition, even if Allah knows it, because He the Exalted loves His servant's humbling himself and displaying his lowliness and need, as Musa said: ﴿My Lord, indeed I am in need of whatever good You send down to me.﴾

Among them: modesty, especially from noble people, is a praiseworthy character.

Among them: reciprocating kindness has always been the custom of the earlier nations.

Among them: if a servant does a deed for Allah the Exalted, and then he receives a reward for it without having intended it as his primary aim, he is not blamed for that. As Musa accepted the recompense of the man of Madyan for his favor, which he had not sought, and his heart had not looked forward to any return.

Among them: the legitimacy of hiring (ijarah, contract of hire), and that it is permissible for the tending of sheep and the like, where work is not measured by fixed quantity but is determined by custom.

Among them: that hiring is permissible with a usufruct (manfa'ah) as the consideration, even if the usufruct is a marriage (bud') [as the dowry].

Among them: that a man's proposal to marry his daughter to a man he chooses is not blameworthy.

Among them: the best hired worker and laborer for a person is one who is strong and trustworthy.

Among them: from noble character is that a person treats his hired worker and servant well, and does not burden him with work; as He said: ﴿I do not want to burden you. You will find me, God willing, among the righteous.﴾

Among them: it is permissible to conclude a contract of hire and other contracts without witnesses; as He said: ﴿And Allah is Witness over what we say.﴾

Among them: the signs and clear miracles which Allah brought about through the hand of Musa: the staff that became a serpent, his hand becoming white without harm, and Allah's protection of Musa and Harun from Pharaoh and from drowning.

Among them: one of the greatest punishments is for a person to be a leader in evil, in proportion to his opposition to the signs and clear proofs of Allah. Just as one of the greatest blessings Allah bestows upon His servant is to make him a leader in good, a guide who is guided.

Among them: what it contains of evidence for the message of Muhammad (ﷺ): for he reported these events in detail, in exact agreement and conforming foundations, relating them in a way that confirms the messengers and supports the manifest truth, without being present at any of those events, nor witnessing any one of those places, nor reciting and studying any of these matters, nor sitting with anyone of the people of knowledge. It is nothing but the message of the Compassionate, the Merciful, and a revelation sent down to him by the Generous, the Bestower, so that he might warn with it a people who were ignorant and heedless of warners and messengers. So may Allah's blessings and peace be upon the one whose mere report indicates that he is the Messenger of Allah, and whose mere command and prohibition alerts enlightened minds that it is from Allah. How much more so, when the reports of the first and last generations agree on the truth of what he brought and its veracity, and the law he brought from the Lord of the worlds, and the noble character with which he was created, which is suitable only for the highest of creation in rank, and the clear victory for his religion and his community, until his religion reached the extent of the night and day, and his community conquered most of the lands of the cities with the sword and the spear, and with their hearts through knowledge and faith. The hostile nations and the disbelieving kings, united in their hostility, have never ceased to target him with a single bow and to plot against him, scheming to extinguish, conceal, and suppress him from the earth, yet he has overwhelmed and surpassed them. He grows only in strength, and his signs and proofs become only more manifest. And at every time there appears from his signs what is a lesson for the worlds, a guidance for the knowing, and light and insight for the discerning. And all praise is due to Allah alone.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 28, verses 1–51 (part 1 of 3)**

Volume Six of *Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman fi Tafsir Kalam al-Mannan* (The Facilitation of the Gracious One's Mercy in the Exegesis of the Words of the Bestower), one of the favours of Allah upon His servant, the son of His servant and the son of His handmaid, Abd al-Rahman ibn Nasir ibn Abd Allah ibn Sa'di.

This surah is Meccan.

[2] ﴿Those﴾ are verses deserving of honour and glorification, ﴿the verses of the Manifest Book﴾, which clarify everything that the servants need: knowledge of their Lord, knowledge of His rights, knowledge of His friends and His enemies, knowledge of His events and His days, and knowledge of the reward of deeds and the recompense of those who labour. This Qur'an has made all of these clear to the utmost degree of clarity, has made them manifest to the servants, and has explained them.

[3] Among the matters that it has made clear is the story of Musa and Fir'awn (Pharaoh). He has presented it and repeated it in a number of places, and in this place he has expounded it, saying: ﴿We recite to you from the news of Musa and Fir'awn in truth﴾. Indeed, their news is strange and their account is wondrous. ﴿For a people who believe﴾: the address is directed to them and the speech is aimed at them, since they possess the faith which leads them to reflect upon it, to receive it with acceptance, and to be guided by the places of lessons, and by it they increase in faith, certainty and goodness, one good leading to another. As for others, they gain from it nothing but the establishment of proof against them. Allah has protected it from them and placed between them and it a veil, so that they do not comprehend it.

[4] The beginning of this story: ﴿Indeed, Fir'awn exalted himself in the land﴾, in his kingdom, his authority, his armies and his tyranny, so he became one of the exalted in it, not one of the lowly in it. ﴿And made its people into sects﴾, that is, into divided groups, whom he manipulated according to his desires and over whom he executed what he willed of his domination and might. ﴿He oppressed a faction among them﴾, and that faction was the Children of Israel, whom Allah had preferred over the worlds, and whom it would have been fitting for him to honour and respect. But he oppressed them to such a degree that he saw they had no strength to prevent him from what he willed concerning them, so he ceased to care for them or concern himself with their affairs. The matter reached the point where ﴿he slaughtered their sons and let their women live﴾, out of fear that they would multiply and overwhelm him in his land and that the kingdom would pass to them. ﴿Indeed, he was among the corrupters﴾, who have no intention of setting right either religion or worldly life. This was part of his corruption in the land.

[5] ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land﴾, by removing from them the causes of their oppression, destroying those who opposed them and forsaking those who were hostile to them, ﴿and to make them leaders﴾ in religion. That cannot be attained while they are oppressed; rather, there must be firm establishment in the land and complete power. ﴿And to make them the inheritors﴾ of the land, those for whom the final outcome is in this world before the Hereafter.

[6] ﴿And to establish them in the land﴾. All these matters are bound up with the will of Allah and have proceeded according to His purpose. ﴿And that We show Fir'awn and Haman﴾, his minister, ﴿and their hosts﴾, by which they roamed and surged, exalted themselves and transgressed, ﴿from them﴾, that is, from this oppressed group, ﴿that which they had feared﴾, namely their expulsion from their homes. For this reason they strove to suppress them, break their power, and kill their sons, who were the very object of this fear. All of this Allah had willed, and when He wills a matter, He facilitates its causes and makes its paths plain. This matter is of that kind, for He decreed and set in motion causes, of which neither His friends nor His enemies were aware, which were a means leading to this goal.

[7] The first step in this was when Allah brought into being His messenger Musa, through whom and by whose means the deliverance of this Israelite people was to be accomplished. This happened at the time of that great terror in which the sons were being slaughtered. He revealed to his mother that she should suckle him and keep him with her. ﴿And when you fear for him﴾, that is, when you sense that someone may bring him to them and you fear for him, ﴿then cast him into the river﴾, that is, the Nile of Egypt, placed inside a sealed chest. ﴿And do not fear, nor grieve; indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers﴾. He gave her the good news that He would return him to her, that he would grow up and be saved from their plotting, and that Allah would make him a messenger. This is among the greatest of noble glad tidings. The giving of this glad tidings to the mother of Musa was so that her heart would be set at rest and her fear calmed.

[8] It seems she feared for him and did what she had been commanded: she cast him into the river, and Allah, exalted is He, guided him until ﴿the people of Fir'awn picked him up﴾, so he became one of their findings, and they were the ones who took charge of him, ﴿that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾, that is, so that the final outcome and consequence of this picking up would be that he became an enemy to them and a grief that would sadden them. This is because caution does not avail against decree, and the one they feared from among the Children of Israel, Allah arranged that he would be their leader, raised under their hands, under their watch and in their care.

Upon reflection and contemplation, you will find within this many benefits for the Children of Israel, the averting of many grievous matters from them and the prevention of many transgressions against them before his mission. Indeed, he became one of the great men of the kingdom, and it was inevitable that he would defend the rights of his people. Moreover, he was a man of lofty resolve and blazing zeal. For this reason the situation of that oppressed people, whose humiliation and degradation had reached the point that Allah has related to us some of it, came to the point that some of its individuals contended with that dominant, exalted people in the land, as will be explained later. This is a prelude to manifestation, for Allah, exalted is He, has the established practice that He makes matters proceed gradually, step by step, and they do not come all at once. His words, ﴿Indeed, Fir'awn, Haman and their hosts were sinners﴾, mean: We willed to punish them for their sin, and to bring about their ruin as a recompense for their scheming and their plotting.

[9] When the people of Fir'awn picked him up, Allah caused the wife of Fir'awn, the virtuous, noble, believing woman Asiya bint Muzahim, to feel compassion for him, and she said: ﴿This is a delight of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him﴾, that is, let him remain with us so that our eyes may be delighted by him and we may be gladdened by him in our lives, ﴿perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son﴾. That is, it is not beyond possibility that he would be like a servant who labours for our benefit and service, or that we would raise him to a higher rank than that, making him a son for us and honouring and exalting him. Allah, exalted is He, decreed that he would benefit the wife of Fir'awn who uttered that statement, for when he became a delight of her eye, she loved him intensely, and he remained for her in the position of a compassionate son until he grew up. Allah gave him prophethood and sent him, and she hastened to accept Islam and faith in him. May Allah be pleased with her and make her pleased. Allah, exalted is He, related these exchanges and disputes concerning Musa: ﴿and they did not perceive﴾ what was decreed by the Pen and carried out by the Decree, namely his arrival at what he arrived at. This is from His subtle kindness, exalted is He, for had they perceived, the matter would have been entirely different for them and for him.

[10] When the mother of Musa was bereaved of him, she grieved intensely, and her heart became empty from the anxiety that had disturbed her in accordance with the human condition, even though Allah had forbidden her from grief and fear and had promised her his return. ﴿She was about to disclose him﴾, that is, to reveal what was in her heart, ﴿had We not bound fast upon her heart﴾, that is, strengthened her, so she was patient and did not disclose him, ﴿that she might be among the believers﴾. Indeed, when a servant is struck by a calamity and is patient and steadfast, his faith increases thereby, and this shows that persistent distress in a servant is evidence of weakness of his faith.

[11] ﴿And she said﴾, the mother of Musa, ﴿to his sister: Follow him up﴾, that is, go and trace his track, and search for your brother without anyone sensing you or perceiving your purpose. So she went to follow him, ﴿and she watched him from a distance while they did not notice﴾, that is, she saw him in a manner as if she were a passer-by with no purpose in it. This is from the completeness of caution and vigilance, for had she seen him and come to them deliberately, they would have suspected that she was the one who had cast him, and they might have resolved to slaughter him as a punishment to his family.

[12] Among the kindnesses of Allah to Musa and his mother was that He prevented him from accepting the breast of any woman. So they took him out to the marketplace, out of compassion for him, and perhaps someone would seek him. His sister came while he was in that condition, ﴿and she said: Shall I direct you to a household who will take him in charge for you, and who will be sincere toward him?﴾ This was their chief aim, for they loved him intensely, and Allah had prevented him from the wet-nurses, so they feared that he would die.

[13] When his sister said to them that statement, which contained encouragement to be cared for by the people of this household with complete protection, custody and sincere counsel for him, they hastened to accept her suggestion, and she informed them and directed them to the people of this household. ﴿So We returned him to his mother﴾, as We had promised her, ﴿that her eye might be delighted and she might not grieve﴾, so that he was raised by her in a manner in which she was secure and at peace, rejoicing in him and receiving a generous wage for it. ﴿And that she might know that the promise of Allah is true﴾: We showed her, as direct sight, some of what We had promised her, so that her heart would be set at rest and her faith increased, and that she would know that the promise of Allah concerning his protection and his prophethood would be fulfilled. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾: when they see that the means is confused, that confusion disturbs their faith, because they do not fully know that Allah, exalted is He, places trials and arduous obstacles before lofty affairs and noble aims.

Musa, upon him be peace, then remained among the family of Fir'awn, being raised in their authority, riding their mounts and wearing their garments, while his mother was content with this, having established that she was his mother by nursing, and his close attachment to her was not regarded as objectionable, [and her tenderness toward him]. Consider this subtle kindness and the protection of His prophet Musa from falsehood in his speech, and the facilitation of the matter by which the bond between him and her was made, the very bond that was manifest to people as nursing, by reason of which he calls her mother. Thus, much of what he and others said concerning all of that was truthful and right.

[14] ﴿And when he reached his full strength﴾, of power, intellect and reason, which is generally about forty years, ﴿and became mature﴾, when those qualities were perfected in him, ﴿We gave him judgment and knowledge﴾, that is, judgment by which he knew the legal rulings of the Sharia and by which he judged among people, and abundant knowledge. ﴿Thus do We recompense the good-doers﴾ in the worship of Allah and who are good to the creation of Allah: He gives them knowledge and judgment in accordance with their goodness. This indicates the perfection of the goodness of Musa, upon him be peace.

[15–17] ﴿And he entered the city at a time of heedlessness among its people﴾, either at the time of midday rest or at other times when they are heedless of going out, ﴿and he found there two men fighting﴾, that is, quarrelling and striking one another. ﴿This one is of his faction﴾, that is, of the Children of Israel, ﴿and this one is of his enemy﴾, the Copts. ﴿So the one of his faction called upon him for help against the one of his enemy﴾, for it had become well known and people knew that he was from the Children of Israel. His appeal to Musa is evidence that he had reached a standing of which Musa was feared and from which hope was held, from the house of the kingdom and its authority. ﴿So Musa struck him﴾, that is, he struck the one from his enemy in response to the Israelite's plea for help, ﴿and so he killed him﴾, that is, caused him to die from that blow, owing to its severity and the strength of Musa. Musa, upon him be peace, then repented of what had happened and ﴿said: This is from the work of Satan﴾, that is, from his adornment and whispering. ﴿Indeed, he is a clear, misleading enemy﴾: for this reason I did what I did, because of his manifest enmity and his eagerness to lead astray. Then he sought forgiveness from his Lord, and ﴿said: My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me﴾, ﴿and He forgave him; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾, especially for those who turn humbly to Him and hasten to repentance and return, as Musa did, upon him be peace. ﴿He said﴾, Musa: ﴿My Lord, by that which You have bestowed upon me﴾, of repentance, forgiveness and abundant blessings, ﴿I will never be a supporter﴾, that is, a helper and aide, ﴿of the criminals﴾, that is, I will not assist anyone in disobedience. This is a promise from Musa, upon him be peace, because of Allah's favour upon him, that he would not assist a criminal as he had done in the killing of the Copt. This indicates that blessings require from the servant the doing of good and the abandonment of evil.

[18–19] When the killing of the one who was from his enemy occurred at his hand, he became ﴿in the city, fearful and watchful﴾: whether the family of Fir'awn would become aware of it or not. He was afraid because he knew that no one among the Children of Israel would dare such an act except Musa. While he was in this condition, ﴿behold, the one who had sought his help the previous day﴾, against his enemy, ﴿was calling out to him﴾ against another Copt. ﴿Musa said to him﴾, rebuking him for his condition: ﴿Indeed, you are clearly misguided﴾, that is, manifestly erring and openly bold. ﴿When he wanted to strike﴾ Musa ﴿the one who was an enemy to them both﴾, that is, to him and to the one who had sought Musa's aid, the dispute between the Copt and the Israelite continued, and the Israelite was calling on Musa for help, so zeal seized him until he resolved to strike the Copt. Then ﴿the man said﴾, the Copt, rebuking him from killing him: ﴿Do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday? You intend nothing but to be a tyrant in the land﴾, for among the greatest marks of a tyrant in the land is the killing of a soul without right. ﴿And you do not intend to be among the reformers﴾: for if you had intended reform, you would have come between me and him without killing anyone. So Musa ceased from killing him and turned back, heeding his admonition and rebuke.

[20] The news spread of what Musa had done in these two incidents, until the chiefs of Fir'awn and Fir'awn himself conspired to kill him and consulted together about this. Allah then arranged for that counselling man, who hastened to inform Musa of what the assembly of their chiefs had agreed upon. He said: ﴿And there came a man from the farthest part of the city, running﴾, that is, running on his feet out of sincere counsel to Musa and fear that they would act against him before he became aware. He said: ﴿O Musa, indeed the chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you, so leave; indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisers﴾. So Musa heeded his counsel.

[21] ﴿So he left it, fearful and watchful﴾ lest the killing befall him. He called upon Allah and ﴿said: My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people﴾. He had repented of his sin, and what he had done was out of anger, without intending to kill; therefore their threat against him was injustice and boldness on their part.

[22] ﴿And when he turned toward Madyan﴾, that is, he set his face toward Madyan, which lies in the south of Palestine, where there was no kingdom of Fir'awn, ﴿he said: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way﴾, that is, the middle of the direct road that leads there with ease and gentleness. So Allah guided him to the right way, and he arrived at Madyan.

[23] ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found upon it a community of people watering﴾ their livestock, for they were people with abundant herds. ﴿And he found beside them two women holding back their flock﴾, that is, keeping their sheep away from the watering places of the people, because they were unable to compete with the men, and because of the stinginess of those men and their lack of manliness in not watering for them. ﴿He said﴾ to them, Musa: ﴿What is your matter?﴾, that is, what is your concern in this condition? ﴿They said: We cannot water until the shepherds have driven off their flocks﴾, that is, it is the custom that we are not able to water until the shepherds have led away their animals. When the place is clear for us, we water, ﴿and our father is an old man﴾, that is, he has no strength to water, so there is no strength among us by which we might prevail, nor do we have men to compete with the shepherds.

[24] Musa, upon him be peace, took pity on them and had compassion for them, ﴿so he watered for them﴾, not seeking any wage from them, nor having any purpose except the countenance of Allah, exalted is He. When he had watered for them, and that was at the time of the intense heat of midday, as indicated by His words ﴿then he withdrew to the shade﴾, resting in those shadows after the fatigue, ﴿and he said﴾ in that state, asking his Lord for sustenance: ﴿My Lord, indeed I am in need of whatever good You send down to me﴾, that is, I am in need of the good that You bring to me and facilitate for me. This is a request from him by his condition, and a request by condition is more eloquent than a request by the tongue of speech.

{25} So he remained in this state, calling upon his Lord and humbly entreating Him. As for the two women, they went back to their father and told him what had happened. Their father sent one of them to Musa, and she came to him "walking shyly" (Qur'an 28:25). This indicates the nobility of her origin and her good character, for modesty is among the virtuous qualities, especially in women. It also indicates that Musa, peace be upon him, in what he did by watering their flock for them, was not in the position of a hired laborer or servant from whom one does not customarily feel shy; rather, he was a man of dignity, whose good character and noble manners she saw, and which made her feel shy before him. She said to him: "Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you with the wage for what you watered for us" (Qur'an 28:25); that is, not as a favor upon you, but rather you were the one who began with kindness towards us, and his intention is only to repay you for your kindness. Musa then responded to her invitation. "So when he came to him and related to him the narrative" (Qur'an 28:25): from the beginning of the cause that led to his flight until he arrived at him. "He said": reassuring his fear and comforting his heart: "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people" (Qur'an 28:25); that is, let your fear and alarm depart, for Allah has delivered you from them, since you have reached this place over which they have no authority.

{26} "One of the two said": that is, one of his two daughters: "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you could hire is the strong and trustworthy" (Qur'an 28:26); that is, make him a hired worker with you, tending and watering the sheep. "Indeed, the best one you could hire is the strong and trustworthy": that is, Musa is the most deserving of those who may be hired, for he combines strength and trustworthiness. The best hired worker is the one who combines these two: strength, meaning the ability to do what he is hired for, and trustworthiness, meaning not betraying what is entrusted to him. These two qualities must be taken into account in everyone who undertakes a task for a person, whether by hire or otherwise, for failure occurs only by lacking one of them or both; but when they are combined, the work is completed and perfected. She said this because she had witnessed Musa's strength and vigor when watering for them, by which she recognized his power, and she had witnessed his trustworthiness and piety, and that he showed mercy to them in a situation where no benefit from them was expected; his intention in this was only the Face of Allah, the Exalted.

{27} So the lord of Madyan said to Musa: "Indeed, I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me for eight years" (Qur'an 28:27); that is, that you become a hired worker for me, "eight years": that is, eight years. "And if you complete ten, it is from you": a voluntary act of yours, nothing being obligatory upon you. "And I do not intend to make it difficult for you" (Qur'an 28:27): so that I would insist on the ten years, or: I do not intend to hire you to burden you with arduous work; rather, I have hired you for easy, light work with no hardship in it. "You will find me, if Allah wills, of the righteous" (Qur'an 28:27): thus he encouraged him by the ease of the work and by good dealing. This indicates that the righteous man should make his character as good as he can, and that the one from whom more is required should strive for greater excellence than others.

{28} So Musa, peace be upon him, responded to his request, saying: "That is [agreed] between me and you" (Qur'an 28:28); that is, the condition you have mentioned, I accept, and it is settled between me and you. "Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there will be no injustice against me" (Qur'an 28:28): whether I fulfill the eight obligatory years or voluntarily add to them. "And Allah is Guardian over what we say" (Qur'an 28:28): a Watcher who observes us and knows what we have contracted.

This man, the father of the two women, the lord of Madyan, is not the well-known Prophet Shu'ayb, as is widely reported among many people, for this is a claim for which no evidence has been given. At most, it is only that Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, had his land in Madyan, and this event took place in Madyan; so where is the necessary connection between the two matters? Furthermore, it is not known that Musa reached the time of Shu'ayb, much less his person! And had that man been Shu'ayb, Allah would have mentioned him, and the two women would have named him. Also, Shu'ayb, peace and blessings be upon him, had his people destroyed by Allah because of their denial of him, and none remained except those who believed in him; and Allah protected the believers in him from being content that the daughters of their prophet be prevented from water and their livestock be driven away until a stranger came and kindly helped them and watered their livestock. Nor would Shu'ayb have been willing for Musa to tend sheep with him and serve him, while Musa was superior to him and higher in rank; unless it is said: this was before Musa's prophethood, so there is no contradiction. In any case, one does not rely on the claim that he was the prophet Shu'ayb without a sound transmission from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. And Allah knows best.

{29} "So when Musa had fulfilled the term" (Qur'an 28:29): it is possible that he fulfilled the obligatory term or the term plus the extra, as is assumed of Musa and of his faithfulness. He longed to reach his family, his mother, his clan, and his homeland, and he thought, given the length of time, that they had forgotten what had happened from him. "He set out with his family" (Qur'an 28:29): intending Egypt. "He perceived" (Qur'an 28:29): that is, he saw, "from the side of the mount a fire" (Qur'an 28:29). "He said to his family: Wait, indeed I have perceived a fire; perhaps I will bring you from it some information, or a burning brand from the fire, that you may warm yourselves" (Qur'an 28:29): for the cold had struck them, and they had lost their way.

{30} "But when he came to it, he was called: O Musa, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds" (Qur'an 28:30): so He informed him of His divinity and lordship, and it follows from this that He commanded him to worship Him and devote himself to Him, as He stated in another verse: "So worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance" (Qur'an 20:14).

{31} "And throw down your staff" (Qur'an 28:31): so he threw it. "But when he saw it moving as if it were a snake" (Qur'an 28:31): it was running swiftly, and it had a frightening form, "as if it were a jann": the great snake. He "turned to flee and did not return" (Qur'an 28:31); that is, he did not come back, because terror had taken hold of his heart. Then Allah said to him: "O Musa, come forward and fear not. Indeed, you are of the secure" (Qur'an 28:31). This is the strongest form of assurance and freedom from fear; for His saying "come forward" requires the command to approach, and obedience to it is obligatory; but his approach might still be while the frightening matter continues; so He said "and fear not," commanding him with two things: to approach, and that no fear be in his heart. But a possibility remains: that he might approach while not afraid, yet not attain protection and security from harm; so He said "indeed, you are of the secure," and then the danger was removed in every respect. So Musa, peace be upon him, came forward, not afraid nor terrified, but reassured and trusting in the report of his Lord; his faith increased and his certainty was complete. This was a sign Allah showed him before his going to Pharaoh, so that he might be in complete certainty, and so that he would be bolder, stronger, and more resolute.

{32} Then He showed him the other sign, saying: "Insert your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without evil" (Qur'an 28:32): that is, put it into your garment; "and draw your arm to your side against fear" (Qur'an 28:32): that is, press your wing, which is your upper arm, against your side, so that dread and fear may depart from you. "These two are proofs from your Lord" (Qur'an 28:32): that is, two decisive arguments from Allah "to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they have been a defiantly disobedient people" (Qur'an 28:32): so mere warning and the command of the messenger will not suffice for them; rather, there must be dazzling signs, if they are to benefit.

{33–34} Musa, peace be upon him, said, apologizing to his Lord, asking Him for help in what he was charged with, and mentioning the obstacles within him so that his Lord might remove what he feared from them: "My Lord, indeed I killed a man among them, so I fear they will kill me. And my brother Harun is more eloquent in speech than I, so send him with me as a supporter" (Qur'an 28:33–34): that is, a helper and aide, to confirm [my words], for when reports converge, the truth is strengthened.

{35} Allah granted his request, saying: "We will strengthen your arm through your brother" (Qur'an 28:35): that is, We will assist you with him and empower you. Then He removed from him the danger of being killed, saying: "And We will give you both authority" (Qur'an 28:35): that is, a power and capability to call with proof and with divine awe against their enemy; "so they will not reach you" (Qur'an 28:35). This is by means of Our signs and what they indicate of the truth, and what they shake in those who encounter them and look upon them; these are what gave you authority and removed from you the plot of your enemy, and they became for you more forceful than armies of great number and equipment. "You two and whoever follows you will be the victorious" (Qur'an 28:35). This was a promise to Musa at that time, when he was alone and solitary; he had returned to his land after having been a fugitive. The circumstances continued to change and affairs kept shifting until He fulfilled His promise to him, granted him authority over the servants and the lands, and he and his followers attained victory and dominance.

{36} So Musa went forth with the message of his Lord. "But when Musa came to them with Our signs as clear evidences" (Qur'an 28:36): manifestly clear in indicating what he told them, with no deficiency or obscurity. "They said": out of wrongdoing, arrogance, and obstinacy: "This is not but fabricated magic" (Qur'an 28:36); as Pharaoh said in that situation, in which the truth had become manifest, had prevailed over falsehood, falsehood had vanished, and the knowledgeable chiefs, who recognized the realities of affairs, submitted to it: "Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic!" (cf. Qur'an 26:49). Yet he was clever but not pure, possessing such deceit, trickery, and scheming as Allah has related to us; and he knew that none had sent down these signs except the Lord of the heavens and the earth, but wretchedness prevails. "And we have not heard of this among our first fathers" (Qur'an 28:36). They lied in this, for Allah sent Yusuf before Musa, as He said: "And Yusuf had already come to you with clear proofs, but you continued in doubt about what he brought you, until when he died, you said: Allah will never send after him a messenger. Thus does Allah leave astray whoever is a transgressor and doubter" (Qur'an 40:34).

{37} "And Musa said" (Qur'an 28:37), when they claimed that what he brought them was magic and error, and that what they were upon was guidance: "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him and who will have the best outcome in the Home" (Qur'an 28:37); that is: if confrontation and the clarification of the clear signs did not benefit you, and you refused except to persist in your error and obstinately cling to your disbelief, then Allah, the Exalted, knows the guided one and others, and who will have the good outcome of the Home, we or you. "Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed" (Qur'an 28:37): so the good outcome of the Home belonged to Musa and his followers, along with success and triumph, while for those there was loss, evil outcome, and destruction.

{38} "And Pharaoh said" (Qur'an 28:38), presumptuously against his Lord and deceiving his foolish people, whose minds were blind: "O chiefs, I know not of any god for you other than me" (Qur'an 28:38); that is: I alone am your god and object of worship, and if there were another god than me, I would have known it! Observe this perfect cautiousness of Pharaoh: he did not say "you have no god other than me!" but was careful and said "I know not of any god for you other than me!" This is because among them he was the learned and distinguished one, whatever he said was the truth, and whatever he commanded they obeyed.

When he uttered this statement, which might admit that there is another god than him, he wished to establish the negation in which that possibility lay, so he said to Haman: "Kindle for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay" (Qur'an 28:38), to make for him bricks of baked clay, "and make for me a tower" (Qur'an 28:38): that is, a high structure, "that I may look at the god of Musa, though I think him [to be] a liar" (Qur'an 28:38). But we will confirm this assumption and show you Musa's lie.

Observe this great audacity against Allah, which no human has reached! He denied Musa, claimed to be god, denied that he had any knowledge of the true God, and took measures to reach the god of Musa; all of this is deception. But how strange are these chiefs who claim to be the great ones of the kingdom managing its affairs: how did this man play with their minds and make fools of their intellects?! This is because of their wickedness, which had become an established trait in them; their religion became corrupt, and then their minds were corrupted too. So we ask You, O Allah, for steadfastness in faith, and that You not cause our hearts to swerve after You have guided us, and that You bestow upon us mercy from You, for You are the Bestower.

{39} Allah the Exalted says: "And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right" (Qur'an 28:39): they were arrogant toward the servants of Allah, inflicted on them the worst torment, and were arrogant toward the messengers of Allah and the signs they brought, denying them and claiming that what they were upon was higher and better than them. "And they thought that to Us they would not be returned" (Qur'an 28:39). Therefore they became bold; had they known or thought that they would be returned to Allah, what they did would not have occurred.

{40} "So We seized him and his soldiers" (Qur'an 28:40) when their obstinacy and transgression persisted, "and We threw them into the sea. So look at the end of the wrongdoers" (Qur'an 28:40): it was the worst end and the most ruinous, one that brought after it a worldly punishment continuous and linked to the punishment of the Hereafter.

{41} "And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire" (Qur'an 28:41); that is, We made Pharaoh and his chiefs leaders who are followed and whose steps are trodden, leading to the abode of disgrace and misery. "And on the Day of Resurrection, they will not be helped" (Qur'an 28:41): against the punishment of Allah; they are the weakest of all in repelling it from themselves, and they have no protector or helper besides Allah.

{42} "And We followed them in this world with a curse" (Qur'an 28:42); that is, We followed them, as an increase in their punishment and disgrace in this world, with a curse by which they are cursed, and among the creatures they have ill repute, detestation, and blame. This is a matter observed: they are the leaders of the cursed in this world and their front ranks. "And on the Day of Resurrection, they will be of the despised" (Qur'an 28:42): those removed far away, whose deeds are loathsome, upon whom gathered the hatred of Allah, the hatred of His creatures, and their own self-loathing.

{43} "And We had already given Musa the Scripture" (Qur'an 28:43): that is, the Torah, "after We had destroyed the former generations" (Qur'an 28:43): whose last in general destruction was Pharaoh and his soldiers. This is evidence that after the revelation of the Torah, the general destruction ceased, and the fighting of disbelievers with the sword was legislated. "As insights for mankind" (Qur'an 28:43): that is, the Book of Allah which He sent down to Musa contains insights for mankind; that is, matters by which they see what benefits them and what harms them, so that the proof is established against the disobedient, and the believer benefits from it, making it a mercy for him and guidance to him on the straight path. For this reason He said: "And guidance and mercy, that they might remember" (Qur'an 28:43).

{44} When Allah had related to His Messenger these unseen reports, He alerted the servants that this is a purely divine report, to which the Messenger has no way of knowing except through revelation. For this reason He said: "And you were not on the western side" (Qur'an 28:44); that is, on the western side of the mount, at the time when We decreed the affair to Musa, "nor were you among the witnesses" (Qur'an 28:44) to it, so that it could be said that it reached you by this route.

{45} "But We produced generations, and the life span grew long for them" (Qur'an 28:45): so knowledge was effaced and its signs forgotten. We therefore sent you at a time when the need for you and for what We taught you and revealed to you was intense. "And you were not a dweller" (Qur'an 28:45): that is, not residing, "among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses" (Qur'an 28:45): that is, teaching them and learning from them, until you reported what you reported of Musa's affair in Madyan. "But We were ever sending [messengers]" (Qur'an 28:45): that is, that report you brought about Musa is a trace of Our sending you and a revelation, with no way for you to know it without Our sending.

{46} "And you were not on the side of the mount when We called" (Qur'an 28:46): Musa, and commanded him to come to the wrongdoing people, convey Our message to them, and show them some of Our signs and wonders, which We have related to you.

The purpose is this: the events that befell Musa (peace be upon him) in these places, which you related exactly as they happened without addition or omission, must be one of two things. Either you were present and witnessed them, or you went to their locations and learned them from their people. In the first case, that would not prove that you are the Messenger of Allah, since reports of what one witnessed or learned by study are common matters not specific to the Prophets. But this matter is known and certain, that it did happen and occurred as it did. Your allies and your enemies both know that you did not witness it. So the second possibility is determined: this came to you from Allah, by His revelation and His sending. Thus the truth of your message is established by definitive proof, and so is Allah's mercy toward His servants through you. For this reason He said:
﴿But it is a mercy from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾; that is, the Arabs and the Quraysh, for the message was unknown to them at the time of the Messenger's sending and for long ages before it. ﴿So that they may remember﴾: distinguishing good and doing it, and distinguishing evil and abandoning it. Since you hold this rank, it was obligatory for them to hasten to believe in you and to give thanks for this blessing, whose worth cannot be measured and whose thanks cannot be fully rendered. His warning to the Arabs does not negate that he was also sent to others, for he is an Arab, the Qur'an revealed to him is in Arabic, and the first to whom he directed his call were the Arabs. So his mission was primarily to them and secondarily to others, as Allah the Exalted said:
﴿Is it a wonder to the people that We revealed to a man from among them: Warn the people?﴾ and ﴿Say: O people, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all.﴾

{47} ﴿And had it not been that a calamity should befall them for what their hands have put forward﴾: of disbelief and disobedience, they would have said: ﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your verses and be among the believers?﴾ That is, We have sent you, O Muhammad, to remove their argument and cut off their pretext.

{48} ﴿But when the truth came to them﴾: which is beyond doubt, ﴿from Us﴾: namely the Qur'an which We revealed to you. ﴿They said﴾: rejecting it and raising objections with what is not a valid objection: ﴿Why was he not given the like of what was given to Musa?﴾ That is, why was not a book sent down from heaven all at once? Now, as for the fact that it is sent down in installments, that does not show it is not from Allah. What proof is there in this? And what doubt is there that it is not from Allah merely because it was sent down piecemeal? Rather, part of the perfection of this Qur'an and of Allah's care for the one to whom it was sent is that it was sent down in parts, so that Allah might strengthen the heart of His Messenger through it, and that the faith of the believers might increase. ﴿And they do not bring you any example but We bring you the truth and the best explanation.﴾ Moreover, their analogy with the Book of Musa is an analogy they themselves have broken. How can they draw an analogy with a book which they disbelieved in and did not believe [in]? For this reason He said: ﴿Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Musa before? They said: Two kinds of magic supporting each other﴾; that is, the Qur'an and the Torah cooperate in their magic and in misleading people. ﴿And they said: Indeed we are disbelievers in both.﴾ Thus it is established by this that these people want to nullify the truth with what is not proof, and they refute it with what cannot be refuted, and they utter contradictory and varying statements. This is the condition of every disbeliever. For this reason He declared that they disbelieved in both books and both messengers.

{49} But is their disbelief in both of them a pursuit of truth and following of something they regard as better than both, or is it merely caprice? Allah the Exalted, binding them to this, said: ﴿Say: Then bring a book from Allah that is better guidance than both of them﴾; that is, better than the Torah and the Qur'an; ﴿I will follow it, if you are truthful.﴾ They have no way, nor does anyone else have a way, to bring the like of these two, for since Allah created the world no books have reached the world like these two in knowledge, guidance, clarity, and mercy to creation. This is from the perfection of fairness on the part of the caller, that he says: My aim is the truth, guidance, and right direction, and I have brought you this book which contains that and agrees with the Book of Musa. Therefore it is incumbent upon all of us to submit to both and follow them insofar as they are guidance and truth. If you bring me a book from Allah that is better guidance than them, I will follow it; otherwise I will not abandon a guidance and truth I know for something other than guidance and truth.

{50} ﴿But if they do not respond to you﴾: and do not bring a book better guidance than them, ﴿then know that they only follow their own desires﴾; that is, know that their abandonment of following you is not because they are going toward a truth they recognize or toward guidance, but is merely following their desires. ﴿And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah?﴾ This is one of the most astray of people, for guidance and the straight path that leads to Allah and to the abode of His honor were presented to him, yet he did not turn to it or incline to it, and his desire called him to take the paths leading to ruin and wretchedness, so he followed it and abandoned guidance. Is there anyone more astray than one described thus? But his wrongdoing, his transgression, and his lack of love for the truth are what made it necessary for him to remain in his error and for Allah not to guide him. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾; that is, those for whom wrongdoing has become a characteristic and obstinacy a description. Guidance came to them and they rejected it, desire presented itself to them and they followed it. They closed upon themselves the doors and paths of guidance, and opened upon themselves the doors and ways of misguidance. So they wander in their error and wrongdoing, and hesitate in their wretchedness and ruin. In His words ﴿But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their desires﴾ there is evidence that everyone who does not respond to the Messenger and goes to a statement contrary to the statement of the Messenger, has not gone to guidance but to desire.

{51} ﴿And We have certainly conveyed the word to them﴾; that is, We followed it up, connected it, and sent it down gradually, out of mercy and kindness toward them, ﴿so that they might remember﴾: when its verses are repeated upon them and its clear proofs descend upon them at the time they need them. Thus its piecemeal descent was a mercy to them. So why do they object to what is for their own benefit?

**Section on mentioning some benefits and lessons in this wondrous story**

Among them: the signs of Allah the Exalted, His lessons and His days among the earlier nations, are only benefited from and illuminated by believers. So a servant's lesson is in proportion to his faith. Allah the Exalted only relates these stories for their sake; as for others, Allah does not regard them, and they have no light or guidance from them.

Among them: when Allah the Exalted wills a matter, He prepares its causes and brings them about gradually, step by step, not all at once.

Among them: an oppressed nation, however weak it may be, should not be overcome by laziness in seeking its rights, nor by despair of rising to the highest matters, especially when they are wronged. Just as Allah rescued the nation of the Children of Israel, a weak nation, from the captivity of Pharaoh and his chiefs, and established them in the land and gave them their country as sovereigns.

Among them: as long as a nation is humiliated and subdued, not taking its right and not speaking it, its affairs of religion and worldly life will not be upheld, and it will have no leadership in them.

Among them: Allah's gentleness toward the mother of Musa, and His easing for her the calamity by the good news that Allah would return her son to her and make him one of the messengers.

Among them: Allah decrees for His servant some hardships in order to bring him greater joy than that, or to ward off from him a greater evil than it. As He decreed for the mother of Musa that intense grief and profound anxiety which was a means for her son to reach her in a way that would calm her soul, cool her eye, and increase her in happiness and joy.

Among them: natural fear of creatures does not contradict faith nor remove it, as happened to the mother of Musa and to Musa himself with those fears.

Among them: faith increases and decreases, and among the greatest things by which faith increases and certainty is completed is patience at times of disturbance and Allah's steadfastness at times of distress. As He said: ﴿Had We not strengthened her heart, she would have been among the believers﴾; that is, so that her faith would increase by that and her heart would be at rest.

Among them: among the greatest blessings of Allah upon His servant and the greatest help to a servant in his affairs is Allah's steadfastness toward him, and His binding of his composure and heart at times of fear and at bewildering matters. For by this he is enabled to speak the right word and do the right deed. Unlike one whose anxiety, terror, and agitation persist; his thinking is lost and his mind is stupefied, so he does not benefit himself in that state.

Among them: even if a servant knows that Allah's decree, destiny, and promise are binding and unavoidable, he should not neglect taking the causes he was commanded to take, and that does not contradict his belief in Allah's report. For Allah promised the mother of Musa that He would return him to her, yet she still strove to return him, and she sent his sister to follow him and seek him out.

Among them: it is permissible for a woman to go out for her needs and to speak with men without objection, as happened with the sister of Musa and the daughter of the man of Madyan.

Among them: it is permissible to take payment for nursing, fostering, and for guiding to one who does such work.

Among them: from Allah's mercy toward His weak servant whom He wishes to honor is that He shows him some of His signs and lets him witness some of His clear proofs, which increase his faith, as Allah returned Musa to his mother, so that she would know that Allah's promise is true.

Among them: it is not permissible to kill a disbeliever who has a covenant by contract or by custom. For Musa (peace be upon him) considered his killing of the Coptic disbeliever a sin, and asked Allah's forgiveness for it.

Among them: whoever kills souls without right is counted among the tyrants who spread corruption in the land.

Among them: whoever kills souls without right, and claims that he intends reform in the land and intimidation of the people of sin, is lying in that, and he is a corrupter. As Allah related the words of the Copt: ﴿You only want to be a tyrant in the land, and you do not want to be among the reformers﴾: in the sense of affirming it to him, not denying it.

Among them: a man informing another of what was said about him, in order to warn him of an evil he might fall into, is not tale-bearing (namimah); rather it may be obligatory, as that man informed Musa, advising and warning him.

Among them: if he fears killing and destruction in remaining, he should not throw himself into ruin nor submit to it, but should leave, as Musa did.

Among them: when two corruptions conflict, and one of them must be committed, he should commit the lighter and safer of the two, as when Musa's affair was between staying in Egypt where he would be killed, or going to distant lands whose road he did not know and had no guide except his Lord. But this situation was more hopeful for safety than the first, so Musa followed it.

Among them: a person examining knowledge when there is need to speak about it, if he has not found one of the two opinions preponderant, should seek guidance from his Lord and ask Him to guide him to the correct one of the two, after intending the truth in his heart and searching for it. For Allah does not disappoint one in this condition, as Musa went out toward Madyan and said: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way.﴾

Among them: compassion toward creation and kindness to those who know and those who do not know are among the characteristics of the prophets, and that among kindness is giving water to livestock and helping the weak.

Among them: it is recommended to make supplication by clarifying and explaining one's condition, even if Allah knows it, because He the Exalted loves His servant's humbling himself and displaying his lowliness and need, as Musa said: ﴿My Lord, indeed I am in need of whatever good You send down to me.﴾

Among them: modesty, especially from noble people, is a praiseworthy character.

Among them: reciprocating kindness has always been the custom of the earlier nations.

Among them: if a servant does a deed for Allah the Exalted, and then he receives a reward for it without having intended it as his primary aim, he is not blamed for that. As Musa accepted the recompense of the man of Madyan for his favor, which he had not sought, and his heart had not looked forward to any return.

Among them: the legitimacy of hiring (ijarah, contract of hire), and that it is permissible for the tending of sheep and the like, where work is not measured by fixed quantity but is determined by custom.

Among them: that hiring is permissible with a usufruct (manfa'ah) as the consideration, even if the usufruct is a marriage (bud') [as the dowry].

Among them: that a man's proposal to marry his daughter to a man he chooses is not blameworthy.

Among them: the best hired worker and laborer for a person is one who is strong and trustworthy.

Among them: from noble character is that a person treats his hired worker and servant well, and does not burden him with work; as He said: ﴿I do not want to burden you. You will find me, God willing, among the righteous.﴾

Among them: it is permissible to conclude a contract of hire and other contracts without witnesses; as He said: ﴿And Allah is Witness over what we say.﴾

Among them: the signs and clear miracles which Allah brought about through the hand of Musa: the staff that became a serpent, his hand becoming white without harm, and Allah's protection of Musa and Harun from Pharaoh and from drowning.

Among them: one of the greatest punishments is for a person to be a leader in evil, in proportion to his opposition to the signs and clear proofs of Allah. Just as one of the greatest blessings Allah bestows upon His servant is to make him a leader in good, a guide who is guided.

Among them: what it contains of evidence for the message of Muhammad (ﷺ): for he reported these events in detail, in exact agreement and conforming foundations, relating them in a way that confirms the messengers and supports the manifest truth, without being present at any of those events, nor witnessing any one of those places, nor reciting and studying any of these matters, nor sitting with anyone of the people of knowledge. It is nothing but the message of the Compassionate, the Merciful, and a revelation sent down to him by the Generous, the Bestower, so that he might warn with it a people who were ignorant and heedless of warners and messengers. So may Allah's blessings and peace be upon the one whose mere report indicates that he is the Messenger of Allah, and whose mere command and prohibition alerts enlightened minds that it is from Allah. How much more so, when the reports of the first and last generations agree on the truth of what he brought and its veracity, and the law he brought from the Lord of the worlds, and the noble character with which he was created, which is suitable only for the highest of creation in rank, and the clear victory for his religion and his community, until his religion reached the extent of the night and day, and his community conquered most of the lands of the cities with the sword and the spear, and with their hearts through knowledge and faith. The hostile nations and the disbelieving kings, united in their hostility, have never ceased to target him with a single bow and to plot against him, scheming to extinguish, conceal, and suppress him from the earth, yet he has overwhelmed and surpassed them. He grows only in strength, and his signs and proofs become only more manifest. And at every time there appears from his signs what is a lesson for the worlds, a guidance for the knowing, and light and insight for the discerning. And all praise is due to Allah alone.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 28, verses 1–51 (part 1 of 3)**

Volume Six of *Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman fi Tafsir Kalam al-Mannan* (The Facilitation of the Gracious One's Mercy in the Exegesis of the Words of the Bestower), one of the favours of Allah upon His servant, the son of His servant and the son of His handmaid, Abd al-Rahman ibn Nasir ibn Abd Allah ibn Sa'di.

This surah is Meccan.

[2] ﴿Those﴾ are verses deserving of honour and glorification, ﴿the verses of the Manifest Book﴾, which clarify everything that the servants need: knowledge of their Lord, knowledge of His rights, knowledge of His friends and His enemies, knowledge of His events and His days, and knowledge of the reward of deeds and the recompense of those who labour. This Qur'an has made all of these clear to the utmost degree of clarity, has made them manifest to the servants, and has explained them.

[3] Among the matters that it has made clear is the story of Musa and Fir'awn (Pharaoh). He has presented it and repeated it in a number of places, and in this place he has expounded it, saying: ﴿We recite to you from the news of Musa and Fir'awn in truth﴾. Indeed, their news is strange and their account is wondrous. ﴿For a people who believe﴾: the address is directed to them and the speech is aimed at them, since they possess the faith which leads them to reflect upon it, to receive it with acceptance, and to be guided by the places of lessons, and by it they increase in faith, certainty and goodness, one good leading to another. As for others, they gain from it nothing but the establishment of proof against them. Allah has protected it from them and placed between them and it a veil, so that they do not comprehend it.

[4] The beginning of this story: ﴿Indeed, Fir'awn exalted himself in the land﴾, in his kingdom, his authority, his armies and his tyranny, so he became one of the exalted in it, not one of the lowly in it. ﴿And made its people into sects﴾, that is, into divided groups, whom he manipulated according to his desires and over whom he executed what he willed of his domination and might. ﴿He oppressed a faction among them﴾, and that faction was the Children of Israel, whom Allah had preferred over the worlds, and whom it would have been fitting for him to honour and respect. But he oppressed them to such a degree that he saw they had no strength to prevent him from what he willed concerning them, so he ceased to care for them or concern himself with their affairs. The matter reached the point where ﴿he slaughtered their sons and let their women live﴾, out of fear that they would multiply and overwhelm him in his land and that the kingdom would pass to them. ﴿Indeed, he was among the corrupters﴾, who have no intention of setting right either religion or worldly life. This was part of his corruption in the land.

[5] ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land﴾, by removing from them the causes of their oppression, destroying those who opposed them and forsaking those who were hostile to them, ﴿and to make them leaders﴾ in religion. That cannot be attained while they are oppressed; rather, there must be firm establishment in the land and complete power. ﴿And to make them the inheritors﴾ of the land, those for whom the final outcome is in this world before the Hereafter.

[6] ﴿And to establish them in the land﴾. All these matters are bound up with the will of Allah and have proceeded according to His purpose. ﴿And that We show Fir'awn and Haman﴾, his minister, ﴿and their hosts﴾, by which they roamed and surged, exalted themselves and transgressed, ﴿from them﴾, that is, from this oppressed group, ﴿that which they had feared﴾, namely their expulsion from their homes. For this reason they strove to suppress them, break their power, and kill their sons, who were the very object of this fear. All of this Allah had willed, and when He wills a matter, He facilitates its causes and makes its paths plain. This matter is of that kind, for He decreed and set in motion causes, of which neither His friends nor His enemies were aware, which were a means leading to this goal.

[7] The first step in this was when Allah brought into being His messenger Musa, through whom and by whose means the deliverance of this Israelite people was to be accomplished. This happened at the time of that great terror in which the sons were being slaughtered. He revealed to his mother that she should suckle him and keep him with her. ﴿And when you fear for him﴾, that is, when you sense that someone may bring him to them and you fear for him, ﴿then cast him into the river﴾, that is, the Nile of Egypt, placed inside a sealed chest. ﴿And do not fear, nor grieve; indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers﴾. He gave her the good news that He would return him to her, that he would grow up and be saved from their plotting, and that Allah would make him a messenger. This is among the greatest of noble glad tidings. The giving of this glad tidings to the mother of Musa was so that her heart would be set at rest and her fear calmed.

[8] It seems she feared for him and did what she had been commanded: she cast him into the river, and Allah, exalted is He, guided him until ﴿the people of Fir'awn picked him up﴾, so he became one of their findings, and they were the ones who took charge of him, ﴿that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾, that is, so that the final outcome and consequence of this picking up would be that he became an enemy to them and a grief that would sadden them. This is because caution does not avail against decree, and the one they feared from among the Children of Israel, Allah arranged that he would be their leader, raised under their hands, under their watch and in their care.

Upon reflection and contemplation, you will find within this many benefits for the Children of Israel, the averting of many grievous matters from them and the prevention of many transgressions against them before his mission. Indeed, he became one of the great men of the kingdom, and it was inevitable that he would defend the rights of his people. Moreover, he was a man of lofty resolve and blazing zeal. For this reason the situation of that oppressed people, whose humiliation and degradation had reached the point that Allah has related to us some of it, came to the point that some of its individuals contended with that dominant, exalted people in the land, as will be explained later. This is a prelude to manifestation, for Allah, exalted is He, has the established practice that He makes matters proceed gradually, step by step, and they do not come all at once. His words, ﴿Indeed, Fir'awn, Haman and their hosts were sinners﴾, mean: We willed to punish them for their sin, and to bring about their ruin as a recompense for their scheming and their plotting.

[9] When the people of Fir'awn picked him up, Allah caused the wife of Fir'awn, the virtuous, noble, believing woman Asiya bint Muzahim, to feel compassion for him, and she said: ﴿This is a delight of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him﴾, that is, let him remain with us so that our eyes may be delighted by him and we may be gladdened by him in our lives, ﴿perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son﴾. That is, it is not beyond possibility that he would be like a servant who labours for our benefit and service, or that we would raise him to a higher rank than that, making him a son for us and honouring and exalting him. Allah, exalted is He, decreed that he would benefit the wife of Fir'awn who uttered that statement, for when he became a delight of her eye, she loved him intensely, and he remained for her in the position of a compassionate son until he grew up. Allah gave him prophethood and sent him, and she hastened to accept Islam and faith in him. May Allah be pleased with her and make her pleased. Allah, exalted is He, related these exchanges and disputes concerning Musa: ﴿and they did not perceive﴾ what was decreed by the Pen and carried out by the Decree, namely his arrival at what he arrived at. This is from His subtle kindness, exalted is He, for had they perceived, the matter would have been entirely different for them and for him.

[10] When the mother of Musa was bereaved of him, she grieved intensely, and her heart became empty from the anxiety that had disturbed her in accordance with the human condition, even though Allah had forbidden her from grief and fear and had promised her his return. ﴿She was about to disclose him﴾, that is, to reveal what was in her heart, ﴿had We not bound fast upon her heart﴾, that is, strengthened her, so she was patient and did not disclose him, ﴿that she might be among the believers﴾. Indeed, when a servant is struck by a calamity and is patient and steadfast, his faith increases thereby, and this shows that persistent distress in a servant is evidence of weakness of his faith.

[11] ﴿And she said﴾, the mother of Musa, ﴿to his sister: Follow him up﴾, that is, go and trace his track, and search for your brother without anyone sensing you or perceiving your purpose. So she went to follow him, ﴿and she watched him from a distance while they did not notice﴾, that is, she saw him in a manner as if she were a passer-by with no purpose in it. This is from the completeness of caution and vigilance, for had she seen him and come to them deliberately, they would have suspected that she was the one who had cast him, and they might have resolved to slaughter him as a punishment to his family.

[12] Among the kindnesses of Allah to Musa and his mother was that He prevented him from accepting the breast of any woman. So they took him out to the marketplace, out of compassion for him, and perhaps someone would seek him. His sister came while he was in that condition, ﴿and she said: Shall I direct you to a household who will take him in charge for you, and who will be sincere toward him?﴾ This was their chief aim, for they loved him intensely, and Allah had prevented him from the wet-nurses, so they feared that he would die.
