{76} He, exalted is He, informs about the condition of Qarun, what he did, what was done to him, and how he was advised and admonished. He says: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa﴾; that is, of the Children of Israel, whom Allah preferred over the worlds and surpassed in their time, and upon whom Allah bestowed what He bestowed. Their condition was suited to uprightness. But this Qarun transgressed against his people and became insolent through the great wealth he had been given, which made him arrogant. ﴿And We had given him of treasures﴾; that is, treasures of wealth, a great deal of them, ﴿so that their keys would weigh down a band of strong men﴾. The "usbah" (band) is from ten to nine to seven or so; that is, the keys to the storehouses of his wealth were so heavy that a strong company could barely carry them. These are only the keys, so what do you think of the storehouses themselves? ﴿When his people said to him﴾, advising him and warning him against insolence: ﴿Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾; that is, do not exult in this great worldly wealth or boast of it, lest it distract you from the Hereafter, for Allah does not love those who exult in it and are absorbed in loving it.

{77} ﴿But seek, through what Allah has given you, the Home of the Hereafter﴾; that is, you have obtained from the means of the Hereafter what others do not have from wealth, so use it to seek what is with Allah, give charity, and do not limit yourself to merely attaining desires and enjoying pleasures. ﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾; that is, We do not command you to give away all your wealth and remain destitute. Rather, spend for your Hereafter and enjoy your world with enjoyment that does not diminish your religion or harm your Hereafter. ﴿And do good﴾ to the servants of Allah ﴿as Allah has done good to you﴾ with these riches. ﴿And seek not corruption in the earth﴾ through arrogance, disobedience to Allah, and preoccupation with blessings to the neglect of the Bestower. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters﴾; rather, He will punish them with the most severe punishment.

{78} So Qarun said, rejecting their advice and being ungrateful for the blessing of his Lord: ﴿I was only given it on knowledge I have﴾; that is, I acquired these riches by my own earnings, my knowledge of the ways of gain, and my skill. Or: on knowledge from Allah of my condition; He knows that I deserve it. So why do you advise me about what Allah has given me? Allah, exalted is He, explains that His giving is not evidence of the good condition of the one given: ﴿Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and more abundant in accumulation?﴾ So what prevents the destruction of Qarun, given that Our custom and way has been to destroy those like him and greater than him when they do what necessitates destruction? ﴿And the criminals will not be asked about their sins﴾; rather, Allah will punish them and torment them for what He knows of them. Even if they ascribe to themselves a good condition and testify to their salvation, their word is not accepted, and that does not avert any punishment from them, because their sins are not hidden, so their denial has no basis.

{79} Qarun continued steadfast in his obstinacy, his oppression, and his refusal to accept the advice of his people, exulting and arrogant, his self pleased with itself and deceived by the wealth he had been given. ﴿So he went out one day in his adornment﴾; that is, in the most splendid state of his worldly life. He had the wealth he had, and he had prepared and beautified himself with the greatest that he could. Such adornment from a man like him would ordinarily be awe-inspiring, combining the adornment, splendor, radiance, brilliance, and pride of the world. Eyes gazed at him in that state, his finery filled hearts, and his adornment captivated souls. The onlookers divided into two groups, each speaking according to the aspiration and desire they had. ﴿Those who desired the life of this world said﴾; that is, those whose wills were attached to it and for whom it was the ultimate object of their desire, having no will for anything else: ﴿Oh, if only we had what Qarun has been given!﴾ of the world, its enjoyments, and its splendor. ﴿Indeed, he is one of great fortune.﴾ They spoke truly that he was one of great fortune, if the matter ended at their desires and if there were no other abode beyond this world. He had been given of it what gave him the utmost enjoyment of worldly bliss, and with it he was able to fulfill all his needs. Thus this great fortune is measured by their aspirations. And an aspiration that makes this its ultimate goal and final object is among the lowest, basest, and most meager aspirations, having no way to rise toward lofty goals and precious objectives.

{80} ﴿And those who had been given knowledge said﴾: those who knew the realities of things and looked at the inner nature of the world while those others looked at its outward appearance: ﴿Woe to you!﴾ Lamenting what they wished for themselves, pitying their state, and disapproving of their words: ﴿The reward of Allah﴾, namely the immediate reward of the sweetness of worship, the love of Him, turning to Him, and devoting oneself to Him, and the deferred reward of Paradise and what is in it, which the souls desire and the eyes delight in, ﴿is better than this which you wished for and desired.﴾ This is the reality of the matter. But not everyone who knows this prefers the higher over the lower, and it is not bestowed or granted to anyone ﴿except the patient﴾, those who restrain themselves in obedience to Allah and from His disobedience and in His painful decrees, and who endure the pulls and desires of the world, lest they distract them from their Lord and come between them and what they were created for. These are the ones who prefer the reward of Allah over the perishing world.

{81} When Qarun's state of insolence and pride reached its end, the world was adorned in his eyes, and his self-admiration grew, the punishment suddenly seized him. ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾, as recompense of the same kind as his deeds. Just as he exalted himself over the servants of Allah, Allah brought him down to the lowest of the low, he and his home, his furnishings, and his goods in which he had been deceived. ﴿He had no company to help him against Allah, nor was he among those who could defend themselves﴾; that is, no group, band, servants, or soldiers, ﴿to aid him besides Allah, nor was he of those who could help themselves﴾; that is, when the punishment came upon him he was neither helped nor able to help himself.

{82} ﴿And those who had wished to be in his place the day before﴾; that is, those who desire the life of this world, who said: Oh, if only we had what Qarun has been given, ﴿began to say﴾, lamenting, taking heed, and fearing that the punishment might befall them: ﴿Woe! It is as if Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it﴾; that is, He restricts provision for whom He wills. We then knew that His extending it to Qarun was not evidence of any good in him, and that we were mistaken in saying: Indeed, he is one of great fortune. ﴿Had not Allah been gracious to us﴾, not punishing us for what we said. Had it not been for His grace and favor, ﴿He would have caused the earth to swallow us.﴾ Qarun's destruction became a punishment for him, a lesson and admonition for others, so that those who had envied him, as you have heard, regretted, and their former thinking changed. ﴿It is as if the disbelievers will not prosper﴾; that is, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

The onlookers divided into two groups, each speaking according to the aspiration and desire they had. ﴿Those who desired the life of this world said﴾; that is, those whose wills were attached to it and for whom it was the ultimate object of their desire, having no will for anything else: ﴿Oh, if only we had what Qarun has been given!﴾ of the world, its enjoyments, and its splendor. ﴿Indeed, he is one of great fortune.﴾ They spoke truly that he was one of great fortune, if the matter ended at their desires and if there were no other abode beyond this world. He had been given of it what gave him the utmost enjoyment of worldly bliss, and with it he was able to fulfill all his needs. Thus this great fortune is measured by their aspirations. And an aspiration that makes this its ultimate goal and final object is among the lowest, basest, and most meager aspirations, having no way to rise toward lofty goals and precious objectives.

{80} ﴿And those who had been given knowledge said﴾: those who knew the realities of things and looked at the inner nature of the world while those others looked at its outward appearance: ﴿Woe to you!﴾ Lamenting what they wished for themselves, pitying their state, and disapproving of their words: ﴿The reward of Allah﴾, namely the immediate reward of the sweetness of worship, the love of Him, turning to Him, and devoting oneself to Him, and the deferred reward of Paradise and what is in it, which the souls desire and the eyes delight in, ﴿is better than this which you wished for and desired.﴾ This is the reality of the matter. But not everyone who knows this prefers the higher over the lower, and it is not bestowed or granted to anyone ﴿except the patient﴾, those who restrain themselves in obedience to Allah and from His disobedience and in His painful decrees, and who endure the pulls and desires of the world, lest they distract them from their Lord and come between them and what they were created for. These are the ones who prefer the reward of Allah over the perishing world.

{81} When Qarun's state of insolence and pride reached its end, the world was adorned in his eyes, and his self-admiration grew, the punishment suddenly seized him. ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾, as recompense of the same kind as his deeds. Just as he exalted himself over the servants of Allah, Allah brought him down to the lowest of the low, he and his home, his furnishings, and his goods in which he had been deceived. ﴿He had no company to help him against Allah, nor was he among those who could defend themselves﴾; that is, no group, band, servants, or soldiers, ﴿to aid him besides Allah, nor was he of those who could help themselves﴾; that is, when the punishment came upon him he was neither helped nor able to help himself.

{82} ﴿And those who had wished to be in his place the day before﴾; that is, those who desire the life of this world, who said: Oh, if only we had what Qarun has been given, ﴿began to say﴾, lamenting, taking heed, and fearing that the punishment might befall them: ﴿Woe! It is as if Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it﴾; that is, He restricts provision for whom He wills. We then knew that His extending it to Qarun was not evidence of any good in him, and that we were mistaken in saying: Indeed, he is one of great fortune. ﴿Had not Allah been gracious to us﴾, not punishing us for what we said. Had it not been for His grace and favor, ﴿He would have caused the earth to swallow us.﴾ Qarun's destruction became a punishment for him, a lesson and admonition for others, so that those who had envied him, as you have heard, regretted, and their former thinking changed. ﴿It is as if the disbelievers will not prosper﴾; that is, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

{83} When Almighty God mentioned Qarun, the worldly goods he was given, and where the outcome of his affair led, and that the people of knowledge said, "The reward of God is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds," He encouraged (people) toward the Hereafter and informed them of the means that lead to it, so He said:

{That is the Abode of the Hereafter}: the one God told of in His Books and His Messengers told of, which has gathered every bliss and from which every disturbance and turbidity has been removed. {We appoint it}: as an abode and a dwelling {for those who do not desire exaltedness in the earth, nor corruption}; that is, they have no desire for it. How then (could they) work for exaltedness in the earth over the servants of God, and arrogance toward them and toward the truth?! {Nor corruption}: this encompasses all acts of disobedience. So, if they have no desire for exaltedness in the earth nor for corruption, it follows that their desire is directed toward God, their aim is the Abode of the Hereafter, and their condition is humility toward the servants of God, submission to the truth, and righteous action. These are the God-fearing, to whom the (good) outcome belongs, and for this reason He said: {And the outcome}; that is, the state of success and triumph that is firm and lasting for whoever fears God Almighty. As for others, even if they attain some prominence and comfort, it does not last long and soon passes away.

It is known from this restriction in the noble verse that those who desire exaltedness in the earth or corruption have no share in the Hereafter, nor any portion from it.

{84} He, exalted is He, informs of the multiplying of His bounty and the perfection of His justice, saying: {Whoever brings a good deed}. He stipulated that the doer himself must bring it, because a person may do a good deed while accompanying it with something that prevents it from being accepted or nullifies it; such a person has not brought a good deed. The good deed (al-hasanah) is a generic noun that encompasses everything that Allah and His Messenger have commanded, whether statements or actions, outward or inward, connected to the right of Allah the Exalted and to the rights of His servants. {Then he will have better than it}, meaning: greater and more magnificent. In the other verse: {he will have ten times the like of it}. This multiplication of the good deed is certain, and there may be attached to it causes by which the multiplication increases, as Allah the Exalted said: {And Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing}, according to the state of the doer, his deed, its benefit, its standing, and its place.

{And whoever brings an evil deed}: and it is everything the Lawgiver has forbidden with a prohibition of unlawfulness (tahrim). {Those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except according to what they used to do}, as the words of Allah the Exalted: {Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like of it, and they will not be wronged} [al-An'am 6:160].

**{85}** He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an for you﴾; that is, He sent it down, prescribed its rulings, made clear in it what is lawful and what is unlawful, and commanded you to convey it to all the worlds and to call all the obligated people to its rulings. It is not befitting His wisdom that this life should be only the worldly life, without the servants being rewarded or punished. Rather, He must return you to a Return (ma'ad) in which the good-doers are repaid for their goodness and the evildoers for their disobedience. I have made the guidance clear to them and explained the method to them. If they follow you, that is their fortune and their happiness. If they refuse anything but to disobey you, to revile what you have brought of guidance, and to prefer the falsehood they have over the truth, then there is no room left for dispute, and nothing remains but the recompense for their deeds by the One who knows the unseen and the witnessed, and who knows the one who is right and the one who is wrong. For this reason He said: ﴿Say: My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in manifest error﴾. He knows that His Messenger is the guided guide, and that his enemies are the astray who lead others astray.

**{86}** ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you﴾; that is, you were not seeking the descent of this Book upon you, nor were you prepared for it, nor did you aspire to it, ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord﴾, toward you and toward the servants. So He sent you with this Book, by which He showed mercy to the worlds, taught them what they did not know, purified them, and taught them the Book and the wisdom, though before that they were indeed in ﴿manifest error﴾. When you know that He sent it down to you as a mercy from Him, you know that everything He commanded and forbade in it is a mercy and a bounty from Allah. So let there be no discomfort in your breast about any part of it, nor should you think that its opponent is more righteous and more beneficial. ﴿So do not be a supporter of the disbelievers﴾; that is, do not be a helper to them in what is among the branches of their disbelief. Among the forms of their support is that one should say about any part of it that it contradicts wisdom, benefit and advantage.

**{87}** ﴿And let them not turn you away from the signs of Allah after they have been sent down to you﴾. Rather, convey them and carry them out, do not care about their scheming, do not let them deceive you away from them, and do not follow their desires. ﴿And call to your Lord﴾; that is, make the call to your Lord the ultimate aim of your intention and the goal of your deeds. Whatever contradicts that, abandon it, whether it be showing off, seeking reputation, or conforming to the aims of the people of falsehood, for that leads to being with them and helping them in their affair. For this reason He said: ﴿And do not be among the polytheists﴾: neither in their polytheism, nor in its branches and offshoots, which are all the acts of disobedience.

**{88}** ﴿And do not invoke with Allah another god﴾. Rather, make your worship sincerely for Allah, for ﴿there is no god except Him﴾. No one deserves to be worshipped, loved and served except Allah, the Perfect, the Everlasting, ﴿everything perishes except His Face﴾. Since everything other than Him is perishing and dissolving, the worship of the perishing falsehood is void, because its end is void and its finality corrupt. ﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾ in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, not to anyone else. So when everything other than Allah is false and perishing, and Allah is the Everlasting, there is no god but Him, to Him belongs the judgment in this world and the Hereafter, and to Him is the return of all creation, so that He may repay them for their deeds, it becomes incumbent upon whoever has intellect to worship Allah alone, with no partner; to act for what brings him near to Allah; to beware of His wrath and punishment; and not to come before his Lord unrepentant, nor turning away from his errors and sins.

The tafsir of Surah al-Qasas is complete.
And to Allah belongs all praise, commendation and glory, always and forever.
